global.title: Global Network

scope.countries: Every Country in the directory, in any state. A Country is the top of the hierarchy; Regions, Cities and Centres each belong to exactly one.
scope.regions: Regions are optional subdivisions of a Country. A Country may have none, and a City may sit directly under its Country.
scope.cities: Cities belong to one Country and, where meaningful, to one of its Regions.
scope.centres: Centres are the organisation's local presences. A Centre names a City, or a Region only, or neither — and a virtual Centre has no physical place at all.

global.denied: You do not have permission to change the Global Network directory.

global.name: Name
global.slugHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It forms the public address; changing it keeps the old address working as a redirect.
global.codeHelp: The two-letter ISO 3166-1 code, for example GB. It is stored in capitals.
global.primaryLocaleHelp: The language this record is first named in. It must have a name in that language.
global.namesHelp: Give the name in each language you have it in. Leave a language empty to give no name in it.
global.countryNone: There are no Countries yet. Create a Country first.
global.chooseCountryFirst: Choose the Country first. The page then offers that Country’s regions.
global.countryFixedHelp: A region or city stays in the Country it was created in. To place it in another Country, archive it and create one there.
global.regionCountryHelp: Choose carefully: a region never leaves the Country it is created in.
global.cityRegionHelp: Only this Country’s regions are offered. Changing it moves every centre in this city with it.
global.cityCountryStepHelp: A city never leaves the Country it is created in. Choosing one reloads the page with that Country’s regions.
global.centreCountryStepHelp: Choosing a Country reloads the page with its cities and regions.
global.centreCountryHelp: Choosing another Country reloads the page with its cities and regions. A move is refused while this centre serves cities; remove them first.
global.centreMoving: This centre will move to the Country shown below when you save. Choose its city or region there.
global.citySearch: Find a city by name or slug
global.citySearchHelp: Narrows the city lists below. At most 300 cities are offered at once; search to reach the rest.
global.localityHelp: Choose a city, or — only when there is no city — a region. Not both: a centre in a city takes its region from that city.
global.centreCityHelp: Cities of the Country above, in any state; a draft or archived city says so.
global.centreRegionHelp: Use only when the centre has no city.
global.virtualHelp: A virtual centre has no physical city, region, coordinates or address. Leave those empty when you tick this.
global.coordinatesHelp: Optional. Decimal degrees exactly as the organisation supplied them, up to six decimal places — both or neither. Nothing is looked up automatically.
global.centreWordsHelp: Fill in each language you have. A language left entirely empty is not shown; a description or address needs a name in the same language.
global.descriptionHelp: A short public description of the centre.
global.addressHelp: The postal address as the organisation supplied it. Leave empty for a virtual centre.
global.contactsHelp: Shown publicly on the centre’s page, in this order. {count} of {limit}.
global.contactsFull: This centre has as many contacts as it can hold. Remove one to add another.
global.contactValueHelp: A website must be a full https:// address. A phone number is shown exactly as given, with its country code where it has one.
global.servedHelp: Further cities in this centre’s Country that it also serves. {count} of {limit}.
global.servedEmpty: This centre serves no further cities.
global.servedFull: This centre serves as many cities as it can. Remove one to add another.
global.addServedHelp: Only cities of this centre’s own Country are offered, and none it already serves.
global.addServedNone: No further cities of this Country are available. Create one, or narrow the city search above.

taxonomy.description: Canonical topics, the content languages the platform publishes in, and editorial tags.

denied.topicProtected: This is a canonical topic. Its slug, place and lifecycle are fixed; its translations are not.
denied.topicArchived: That topic is archived. Restore it first.
denied.topicHasActiveChildren: This topic still has active child topics. Archive or move them first.

topics.title: Topics
topics.description: The canonical subject taxonomy. Every topic has a stable slug, a place in the hierarchy and a name in each interface language.
topics.caption: Topics at this level, in display order
topics.name: Name
topics.canonicalNote: This is one of the canonical top-level topics. Its slug, its place in the hierarchy and its lifecycle are fixed foundation data. Its names and descriptions can be translated here.
topics.shownInFallback: Shown in {locale} — no translation for this language yet.
topics.noChildren: No topics at this level yet. Create one below.
topics.createHere: The new topic will be created under {parent}.
topics.slugHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. This permanent identifier appears in links, so choose it carefully.
topics.fallbackNameHelp: Required. Every other language falls back to this name when it has no translation of its own.
topics.descriptionHelp: Optional. Leave it empty rather than writing a placeholder.
topics.translationsHelp: A topic is named separately in each interface language. The {locale} name is required; the others are optional and fall back to it.
topics.moveHelp: Choose where this topic sits. A topic cannot be moved beneath one of its own descendants.
topics.archiveHelp: Archiving retires a topic without deleting it. Topics are never deleted, so nothing that refers to one can be left pointing at nothing.

mapping.title: Topic mapping
mapping.description: Which kinds of content can be classified by a topic, and how that classification is enforced by the database.
mapping.none: Nothing can be assigned a topic yet.
mapping.noneDetail: Topic assignment belongs to the part of the platform that owns the content being classified — articles, Quran, Hadith, Fatawa, courses and the rest. None of those has been built yet, so there is nothing to assign a topic to. This page lists real relationships as each one arrives.
mapping.enforced: The database enforces {count} typed topic-assignment relationships.
mapping.complete: Every detected relationship has real foreign keys at both ends.
mapping.incomplete: {count} detected relationships are incomplete because they have no real target foreign key.
mapping.ruleTitle: How a new kind of content gets topics
mapping.ruleOne: The part of the platform that owns the content creates its own relationship table, with a real reference to the topic and a real reference to its own record.
mapping.ruleTwo: It owns that table for its whole life, including what happens when a record is removed. Taxonomy never writes another area’s records.
mapping.ruleThree: It reads topics through the taxonomy service, never the database directly.
mapping.ruleProhibition: A single shared table holding a record type and an identifier is deliberately not offered. The database cannot enforce such a reference, so it would leave classifications pointing at content that no longer exists.

languages.title: Content languages
languages.description: The languages the platform publishes content in. A work written in Urdu is Urdu content whichever language the site is being read in.
languages.notInterfaceLocale: These are content languages, not site languages. The site is read in English, Urdu and Arabic, and nothing on this page changes that. Adding a content language here makes it available to describe content; it does not add a version of the site.
languages.caption: Content languages
languages.codeHelp: A standard language tag in lowercase, such as ur, ar or pa-arab.
languages.nativeNameHelp: Written in the language’s own script. This is what readers of that language will see.
languages.directionHelp: How text in this language is written. This describes the content, not the site.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Free-form editorial labels. Useful for grouping things loosely; never a substitute for a topic.
tags.notTopics: Tags are not topics. They have no hierarchy, no curation and no guarantees — if something needs to be findable by subject, give it a topic.
tags.caption: Tags
tags.label: Label
tags.labelHelp: What editors will see. Any script.
tags.slugHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. This is what makes two editors typing the same tag produce one tag.
tags.searchHelp: Matches the beginning of a slug or a label.

persons.biographyHelp: Optional. Leave it empty rather than writing a placeholder.

editor.capabilitiesCaption: Capabilities and the permission each is derived from
editor.profilesHelp: One person may hold any combination of the four. Each has its own status, and adding one grants nothing.

editor.qualificationsHelp: Record only what the organisation has confirmed. This platform verifies nothing.
editor.facetBiographyHelp: What a prospective student reads. Separate from the main biography above.
editor.subjectsHelp: Written out in this language. Subject classification arrives with a later phase.

Choosing or changing it is an ordinary edit: it returns the event to draft and needs fresh review. An archived Centre stays named only while it is left unchanged.

editorial.fold: If the clock repeats this hour

editorial.foldLater: The second time (after the clocks go back)
editorial.moreOccurrences: Save to add more occurrences, up to twelve.

privacy.exportSaved: Bookmarks, notes and your private collections
privacy.exportHistory: Reading and watch history, and your Quran reading position
privacy.exportSettings: Your interests and goals, and your history and notification settings
privacy.exportScope: Saved items are listed by reference, not as copies of the content. Your account details and your questions are not part of this file.
privacy.closureBody: Closing your account removes everything listed above — saved items, notes, collections, history, your reading position, interests, notifications, your course enrolments, lesson progress and trial-class requests. It also withdraws any membership application still in progress; it does not end a Membership you hold. Closing is done from your Security settings, with your password.
privacy.newsletterBody: The newsletter is independent of your account: signing up for an account never subscribes you, and closing it does not unsubscribe you. Manage it from the links in its emails.
privacy.learningExportBody: Download a copy of what Learning keeps for your account, as a separate JSON file:
privacy.learningExportContents: Your course enrolments, the lessons you marked complete, your trial-class requests, your trial bookings, the classes you took part in or taught, your attendance, and any teaching windows and scopes of your own — listed by reference, never as copies of the courses and never a meeting link.
privacy.messagingExportBody: Download a copy of what Messaging keeps for your account, as a separate JSON file:
privacy.messagingExportContents: The conversations you take part in, the messages you sent with their text, the details of the files you attached (never the files themselves), how far you have read, the people you blocked and the reports you made. Messages other people sent are never included.
privacy.messagingExportClosure: Closing your account closes your conversations and removes your read positions, any blocks between you and others, and files you uploaded but did not send. The person you were talking to may still be able to read what you both wrote, but cannot reply. A conversation is removed once nobody left can read it — unless a report refers to it, in which case it is kept as evidence.
privacy.membershipExportBody: Download a copy of what Membership keeps for your account, as a separate JSON file:
privacy.membershipExportContents: Your membership applications and Memberships — the type each one is for, its status, who withdrew or ended it, and its dates — listed by reference, never with the types’ descriptions.
privacy.membershipExportClosure: Closing your account withdraws any membership application still in progress. It does not end a Membership you hold: that is an organisational relationship, which you can end from My Membership.

process.close: You can end a Membership from My Membership at any time. Closing your account on this website withdraws any application still in progress, but does not end a Membership.

failure.applicantClosed: The applicant’s account is closed, so the application can’t be taken under review or approved. It can still be not approved.
failure.incomplete: A type can be published only once it has words in its primary language.
failure.limit: No more types can be created: the limit has been reached.
failure.rateLimited: Too many requests in a short time. Please wait and try again.
failure.load: This can’t be shown right now. Please try again later.
failure.noSession: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
failure.secondFactorRequired: Finish setting up two-step verification first.

types.title: Membership types and members
types.description: Only published types appear on the public Membership page and take applications.
types.heading: Types
types.empty: No type of membership has been created yet.
types.caption: Types of membership, in display order

fields.primaryLocaleHelp: The language the type is first written in. Its words in this language are needed for publication, and are shown wherever another language has none.
fields.displayOrderHelp: Lower numbers are listed first, from 0 to 9999.
fields.title: Title
fields.guidanceHelp: Short, practical guidance for applicants. Leave it empty for none.

explain.published: Publishing lists the type on the public Membership page and lets people apply. Its primary language must have words.
explain.archived: Archiving removes the type from the public page and stops new applications and approvals. Existing Memberships are unchanged, and the type can be published again.

labels.heading: Words in each language
labels.help: Each language is saved on its own. Where a language has no words, public pages show the primary language’s words with a notice.
labels.missing: No words in this language yet.

create.heading: Create a type
create.help: A new type starts as a draft, written in its primary language. Add other languages and publish it from its editor.

members.heading: Members
members.description: People who hold, or held, a Membership, most recently begun first. Listing members is recorded in the audit log.
members.forType: Only members of the type being edited are shown.
members.closeConfirm: I want to end this Membership. It cannot be reopened; the person can apply again, and their account is not affected.

applications.title: Applications
applications.description: Oldest first. Listing applications is recorded in the audit log.
applications.invalidFilter: That type filter isn’t recognised, so nothing is listed.
applications.caption: Applications — {status} — oldest first

application.title: Application
application.audited: Opening an application is recorded in the audit log: who opened it, and when.
application.membershipCreated: A Membership began on approval — see the members of this type
application.terminal: This application is finished and can no longer change.

review.heading: Start the review
review.help: The applicant is told by email that their application is being reviewed. A decision can be made only after the review has started.
review.confirm: I am starting the review of this application.

decide.heading: Decision
decide.help: Approving begins a Membership of this type for the applicant. Not approving finishes the application, and the person may apply again. The applicant is told by email either way.
decide.approveConfirm: I approve this application, and a Membership will begin.
decide.rejectConfirm: I do not approve this application.
